info.description:
# Introduction

This API is documented in **OpenAPI format** and describe the REST API of the **Semaphore relay proxy**.

The relay proxy is a component to evaluate your feature flags remotely when using **Semaphore**.  
This API is mostly used by all the OpenFeature providers.
info.title: Semaphore relay proxy endpoints

post.description:
Validates the flag file sent in the body of the request, using the same rules as the
`goff lint` command.
The flag file is not loaded, nothing is changed on the flags served by the relay proxy.
The format of the body is selected with the `Content-Type` header (`application/json`,
`application/yaml`, `application/x-yaml`, `text/yaml` or `application/toml`).
The maximum size of the body is configurable per format with `server.validateFlags`
(defaults: 1 MiB for JSON, 64 KiB for YAML and TOML).

422.description: At least one flag is invalid

post.description:
This endpoint is used to force the refresh of the flags in the cache.
The relay polls the control plane at once, through the poll of its schedule: calls that arrive together
share one poll. The answer tells what the poll found: its result, the generation the relay holds and
whether the poll changed it. A failed poll is an answer with its reason, not an error of the request.
Only an admin key may call it.
post.summary: This endpoint is used to force the refresh of the flags in the cache.

get.description:
This endpoint is provided by the standard library pprof handlers.
To know more please check this blogpost from the GO team https://go.dev/blog/pprof.
Visit the page /debug/pprof/ to see the available endpoints, all endpoint are not in the OpenAPI documentation because they are standard pprof endpoints.
This endpoint is only available in debug mode.

Making a **GET** request to the URL path `/health` will tell you if the relay proxy is ready to
serve
traffic.

This is useful especially for loadbalancer to know that they can send traffic to the service.

Making a **GET** request to the URL path `/info` will give you information about the actual state
of the relay proxy.

As of Today the level of information is small be we can improve this endpoint to
returns more
information.
200 `{"live": true}` while the process serves. It never depends on the control plane or any flag set. Served by the config v2 runtime. No API key.
This endpoint is providing metrics about the relay proxy in the prometheus format.

post.description:
Making a **POST** request to the URL `/ofrep/v1/evaluate/flags` will give you the value of the list
of feature flags for this evaluation context.

If no flags are provided, the API will evaluate all available flags in the configuration.

The key is optional when a flag set is published without API keys (the public flags): a request without a key is then served by those flags. Without such a flag set every request needs a key. A wrong key is always refused.

get.description:
**GET** request to the URL `/openfeature/v0/manifest` returns the project manifest
containing active flags. Archived flags are excluded.

The key is optional when a flag set is published without API keys (the public flags): a request without a key is then served by those flags. Without such a flag set every request needs a key. A wrong key is always refused.
get.summary: GetManifest is a GET endpoint to return the flags configured in Semaphore.

get.description: 200 `{"ready": true, "state": "empty|serving|degraded"}` when the relay is able to serve, else 503 with a reason. Once ready the relay stays ready until shutdown. Served by the config v2 runtime. No API key.
200 once the first bootstrap round has ended, else 503 `{"ready": false, "reason": "starting"}`. Served by the config v2 runtime. No API key.

Server-Sent Events endpoint pushing flag change notifications, following OpenFeature ADR-0008.
It is advertised in the `eventStreams` field of the OFREP bulk evaluation response.
Each event is sent as `event: message` with a `model.OFREPSSEEvent` JSON payload,
a `refetchEvaluation` event means that the provider must re-fetch its evaluations.
The stream also sends SSE comment lines (`: connected` when the connection opens,
`: heartbeat` every 30 seconds), they are ignored by SSE clients.
The full URL (including query string) is sensitive and must not be logged
or persisted by intermediaries.

The key is optional when a flag set is published without API keys (the public flags): a request without a key is then served by those flags. Without such a flag set every request needs a key. A wrong key is always refused.

200.description: SSE stream of OFREP flag change events

get.summary: SSE endpoint to be notified about flag changes

get.description:
This endpoint is a websocket endpoint to be notified about flag changes;
every change pushes a notifier.DiffCache message to the client.
When disableFlagDetailsInStream is true, values are empty objects.

The key is optional when a flag set is published without API keys (the public flags): a request without a key is then served by those flags. Without such a flag set every request needs a key. A wrong key is always refused.
get.summary: Websocket endpoint to be notified about flag changes

post.description:
Making a **POST** request to the URL `/v1/allflags` will give you the values of all the flags for
this user.

To get a variation you should provide information about the user.
For that you should provide some user information in JSON in the request body.

The key is optional when a flag set is published without API keys (the public flags): a request without a key is then served by those flags. Without such a flag set every request needs a key. A wrong key is always refused.

requestBody.description: Evaluation context to challenge against the flags.

post.summary: All flags variations for a user

post.description:
This endpoint is receiving the events of your flags usage to send them in the data collector.

It is used by the different Open Feature providers to send in bulk all the cached events to avoid
to lose track of what happen when a cached flag is used.

The key is optional when a flag set is published without API keys (the public flags): a request without a key is then served by those flags. Without such a flag set every request needs a key. A wrong key is always refused.

requestBody.description: List of flag evaluation that be passed to the data exporter

post.summary: Endpoint to send usage of your flags to be collected

post.description:
Making a **POST** request to the URL `/v1/feature/<your_flag_name>/eval` will give you the value of
the
flag for this user.

To get a variation you should provide information about the user:
- User information in JSON in the request body.
- A default value in case there is an error while evaluating the flag.

Note that you will always have a usable value in the response, you can use the field `failed` to know if
an issue has occurred during the validation of the flag, in that case the value returned will be the
default value.

The key is optional when a flag set is published without API keys (the public flags): a request without a key is then served by those flags. Without such a flag set every request needs a key. A wrong key is always refused.

requestBody.description: Evaluation context and default value for the flag.

get.description:
Making a **GET** request to the URL `/v1/flag/change` will give you the hash of the current
configuration, you can use this hash to know if the configuration has changed.

The key is optional when a flag set is published without API keys (the public flags): a request without a key is then served by those flags. Without such a flag set every request needs a key. A wrong key is always refused.
